definitions.explanation: The order of roads or paths to follow to reach a destination. Refers both to the physical route and to verbal or written directions explaining how to get somewhere.

examples.japanese: {道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}えてください。
{地図|ちず}で{道順|みちじゅん}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked the route on the map.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}からホテルまでの{道順|みちじゅん}をメモに{書|か}いておいた。
examples.english: I wrote down the directions from the station to the hotel on a memo.

notes:
Combines {道|みち} (road) and {順|じゅん} (order/sequence). Emphasizes the step-by-step order of the route rather than just the destination.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}える — to give directions
- {道順|みちじゅん}を{調|しら}べる — to look up directions
- {道順|みちじゅん}を{確認|かくにん}する — to confirm the route
- {道順|みちじゅん}を{間違|まちが}える — to take the wrong route

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ルート — route (loanword, often for planned travel or hiking routes)
- {行|い}き{方|かた} — how to get there (more conversational)
- {経路|けいろ} — route, path (more formal/technical, also used for data routes)
